ENDPOINT BENCHMARK — ENTITY SPECIFICATIONS
==========================================

Task: for EACH entity below, create a complete GraphQL CRUD endpoint
(create, list, get by key, update, remove) following the project's
architecture and conventions. Every endpoint must include:
  - unit tests for the service layer
  - e2e tests driving the full CRUD cycle through /graphql
  - a Bruno request collection (bruno/<entity>/)

Definition of done (per endpoint, all four green):
  pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm test:e2e

Field notation: name: type, constraints
  - "unique" fields are the lookup keys for get/remove
  - "default X" fields are optional on create
  - "optional" fields are nullable
  - "embedded" objects are sub-documents stored inside the entity

------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Author (collection: authors)  [reference — already implemented in both arms]
   - authorId: number, required, unique
   - fullName: string, required
   - email: string, required, unique
   - country: string, optional
   - active: boolean, required, default true

2. Book (collection: books)
   - isbn: string, required, unique
   - title: string, required
   - pages: number, required
   - publishedAt: date, optional
   - inPrint: boolean, required, default true

3. Category (collection: categories)
   - code: string, required, unique
   - name: string, required
   - description: string, optional
   - enabled: boolean, required, default true

4. Supplier (collection: suppliers)
   - supplierId: number, required, unique
   - name: string, required
   - email: string, required, unique
   - phone: string, optional

5. Warehouse (collection: warehouses)  [has embedded object]
   - code: string, required, unique
   - name: string, required
   - capacity: number, required
   - location: embedded, required
       - street: string, required
       - city: string, required
       - latitude: number, required
       - longitude: number, required

6. Employee (collection: employees)
   - employeeId: number, required, unique
   - fullName: string, required
   - email: string, required, unique
   - hiredAt: date, required
   - remote: boolean, required, default false

7. Review (collection: reviews)
   - reviewId: number, required, unique
   - rating: number, required
   - comment: string, optional
   - verified: boolean, required, default false
   - reviewedAt: date, required

8. Coupon (collection: coupons)
   - code: string, required, unique
   - discount: number, required
   - expiresAt: date, required
   - active: boolean, required, default true

9. Invoice (collection: invoices)  [has embedded object]
   - invoiceNumber: number, required, unique
   - total: number, required
   - issuedAt: date, required
   - paid: boolean, required, default false
   - billing: embedded, required
       - street: string, required
       - city: string, required
       - zipCode: string, required

10. Shipment (collection: shipments)  [has embedded object]
    - trackingCode: string, required, unique
    - weight: number, required
    - shippedAt: date, optional
    - delivered: boolean, required, default false
    - destination: embedded, required
        - street: string, required
        - city: string, required
        - country: string, required

11. Payment (collection: payments)
    - paymentId: number, required, unique
    - amount: number, required
    - method: string, required
    - processedAt: date, optional
    - confirmed: boolean, required, default false

12. Ticket (collection: tickets)
    - ticketNumber: number, required, unique
    - subject: string, required
    - priority: number, required
    - openedAt: date, required
    - open: boolean, required, default true

13. Event (collection: events)
    - slug: string, required, unique
    - title: string, required
    - startsAt: date, required
    - seats: number, required
    - published: boolean, required, default false

14. Subscription (collection: subscriptions)
    - subscriptionId: number, required, unique
    - plan: string, required
    - startedAt: date, required
    - renewals: number, required, default 0
    - active: boolean, required, default true

15. Vehicle (collection: vehicles)
    - plate: string, required, unique
    - brand: string, required
    - model: string, required
    - year: number, required
    - electric: boolean, required, default false

10	// Define the base structure for repository response types.
11	type QueryResponse<T> = T | null;
12	
13	// GraphQL input DTOs arrive as class instances whose declared-but-unset fields
14	// are own properties set to undefined (ES2022+ class fields); mongoose 9 no
15	// longer strips undefined from filters — it matches them as null.
16	const omitUndefined = <T extends object>(obj: T): T =>
17	  Object.fromEntries(
18	    Object.entries(obj).filter(([, value]) => value !== undefined),
19	  ) as T;
20	
21	// Define a type for projection and query options.
22	interface FindOptions<T> extends QueryOptions<T> {
23	  projection?: Partial<Record<keyof T, 1 | 0>>;
24	}
25	
26	// Abstract repository class with improved type safety.
27	export abstract class AbstractRepository<TDocument> {
28	  protected constructor(
29	    protected readonly model: Model<TDocument>,
30	    private readonly connection: Connection,
31	  ) {}
32	
33	  /**
34	   * Create a new document.
35	   * @param document - The document to be created.
36	   * @param options - Additional save options.
37	   */
38	  async create<TCreate = TDocument, TResponse = TDocument>(
39	    document: TCreate,
40	    options?: SaveOptions,
41	  ): Promise<TResponse> {
42	    const createdDocument = new this.model<TCreate>(document);
43	    return (await createdDocument.save(options)) as TResponse;
44	  }
45	
46	  /**
47	   * Find a single document by filter.
48	   * @param filterQuery - The filter query to find the document.
49	   * @param options - Additional query options.
50	   */
51	  async findOne<TProjection = TDocument>(
52	    filterQuery: QueryFilter<TDocument>,
53	    options?: FindOptions<TDocument>,
54	  ): Promise<QueryResponse<TProjection>> {
55	    const { projection, ...queryOptions } = options || {};
56	    return this.model.findOne(omitUndefined(filterQuery), projection, {
57	      lean: true,
58	      ...queryOptions,
59	    });
60	  }
61	
62	  /**
63	   * Find multiple documents by filter.
64	   * @param filterQuery - The filter query to find documents.
65	   * @param options - Additional query options and projections.
66	   */
67	  async findMany<TProjection = TDocument>(
68	    filterQuery: QueryFilter<TDocument> = {},
69	    options?: FindOptions<TDocument>,
70	  ): Promise<TProjection[]> {
71	    const { projection, ...queryOptions } = options || {};
72	    return this.model.find(omitUndefined(filterQuery), projection, {
73	      lean: true,
74	      ...queryOptions,
75	    });
76	  }
77	
78	  /**
79	   * Update a single document based on a filter query.
80	   * @param filterQuery - The filter to identify the document.
81	   * @param document - The document to update.
82	   * @param options - Additional query options.
83	   */
84	  async update<TUpdate = Partial<TDocument>, TResponse = TDocument>(
85	    filterQuery: QueryFilter<TDocument>,
86	    document: TUpdate,
87	    options: QueryOptions<TDocument> = {},
88	  ): Promise<QueryResponse<TResponse>> {
89	    const defaultOptions = {
90	      lean: true,
91	      upsert: false,
92	      returnDocument: 'after' as const,
93	    };
94	
95	    return this.model.findOneAndUpdate(
96	      omitUndefined(filterQuery),
97	      omitUndefined(document as UpdateQuery<TDocument>),
98	      {
99	        ...defaultOptions,
100	        ...options,
101	      },
102	    ) as unknown as Promise<QueryResponse<TResponse>>;
103	  }
104	
105	  /**
106	   * Remove a single document by filter query.
107	   * @param filterQuery - The filter query to identify the document to remove.
108	   */
109	  async remove<TResponse = TDocument>(
110	    filterQuery: QueryFilter<TDocument>,
111	  ): Promise<TResponse | null> {
112	    // Using type assertion to specify the type explicitly
113	    const deletedDocument = (await this.model.findOneAndDelete(
114	      omitUndefined(filterQuery),
115	      {
116	        lean: true,
117	      },
118	    )) as unknown as TResponse | null;
119	    return deletedDocument;
120	  }

All 14 entities from `entities-benchmark.txt` are implemented following the Author reference architecture, and the full DoD passes cleanly:

```
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit  ✓
pnpm lint                ✓ (0 errors)
pnpm test                ✓ (16 suites / 76 tests)
pnpm test:e2e             ✓ (16 suites / 76 tests, against real MongoDB)
```

**What was built**, per entity (Book, Category, Supplier, Warehouse, Employee, Review, Coupon, Invoice, Shipment, Payment, Ticket, Event, Subscription, Vehicle):
- GraphQL resolver, service, repository, module, DTOs (create/get/update), entity, Mongoose schema
- Embedded sub-documents for Warehouse (`location`), Invoice (`billing`), Shipment (`destination`) — each with its own `ObjectType`/`InputType` and a proper nested Mongoose sub-schema (avoiding the `type:`-key ambiguity gotcha)
- Unit tests for the service layer (mocked repository)
- e2e tests driving full CRUD through `/graphql` against a live MongoDB
- A 5-request Bruno collection per entity (`bruno/<entity>/`)
- `app.module.ts` wired up with all 14 new modules
